source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Heat exhaustion.","B":"Heat stroke.","C":"Simple dehydration without heat injury.","D":"A normal response to strenuous exercise."}}
source_row.rationale: Very high core temperature accompanied by central nervous system dysfunction such as confusion is characteristic of heat stroke, a life-threatening emergency requiring rapid cooling and emergency care. Option B is correct. Heat exhaustion and uncomplicated dehydration do not account for this severe hyperthermia with altered mental status.
source_row.source_detail: Heat Stroke section: very high body temperature with central nervous system dysfunction such as confusion, altered mental status or loss of consciousness is a medical emergency requiring emergency services and rapid cooling. source_row.stem: A client exercising in extreme heat has a core temperature of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and confusion. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
